ordered_diagnoses: Vascular Tumor of the Thyroid with Metastasis

candidates.name: Vascularized Thyroid Cancer (VTC) metastasis
support_spans: Endoscopic examination found a voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities.
Confirmed a hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Costal Biopsy: 'Pointed to VTC metastasis'
Sinonasal Tumor Biopsy: 'Confirmed VTC metastasis'
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and diagnostic results are consistent with VTC metastasis.

candidates.name: Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma
support_spans: Serum Thyroglobulin: '4432 ng/mL (significantly elevated)'
Radioiodine Scintigraphy: 'Found considerable uptake regarding rib and vertebral lesions.'
contradict_spans: The sinonasal tumor had low uptake, indicative of thyroid tissue with low iodine avidity
candidates.why: The significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin and radioiodine scintigraphy results suggest papillary thyroid carcinoma.

candidates.name: Vascular Tumor of the Thyroid with Metastasis

Confirmed a hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Costal Biopsy: 'Pointed to VTC metastasis'
contradict_spans: The sinonasal tumor had low uptake, indicative of thyroid tissue with low iodine avidity

candidates.name: Multiple Myeloma
support_spans: Enhanced CT scan showed a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity, on the left thyroid, the fifth rib, and the L4 vertebra
candidates.why: The presence of multiple lesions in the ribs and vertebrae could suggest a diagnosis of multiple myeloma, although the significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin levels make this less likely.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may deserve minority protection because it is a rare cause of multiple bone lesions and may be easily missed if not considered in the differential diagnosis.
